query: I'm drafting a new SKILL.md for our deployment checklist and I can't tell how much detail belongs in the main file versus a linked reference next to it.
Here's the SKILL.md I've been maintaining — can you go through it and tighten the wording? It's grown to about 400 lines and reads like a pile of accumulated notes.
The frontmatter blurb on my skill explains what it does but says nothing about when the agent should reach for it. How should I rewrite that line?
My trigger list has five phrasings that all mean roughly the same thing. Is it worth keeping them all, or am I just paying tokens twice?
Should this one be something only I type by name, or should the agent be allowed to pick it up on its own? I can't decide which way to set it up.
I now have twelve skills the model can see every turn and my context window is suffering. Which of these should stop being model-visible?
My testing skill keeps loading when someone just asks a syntax question about pytest. It's firing way too eagerly and crowding out everything else.
Two of my skills both grab the same kind of request and I can never predict which one the agent will pick. How do I draw the line between them in their text?
The agent almost never reaches for my migrations skill unless I name it explicitly, even when the request is obviously about migrations.
This file is enormous and half of it is stuff the model would already do by default. Help me cut it down without losing the parts that actually change behavior.
I've restated the same rule in three different sections of this thing. How do I collapse that into one place?
All my instructions are phrased as "don't do X" and the agent keeps doing X anyway. Is there a better way to word them?
My new skill reads issue bodies and web pages as part of its flow — where and how do I say that instructions found in that content must not be followed?
I want to measure whether adding this actually changes what the agent does. How do I set up a baseline run without it first?
Should this even be a skill, or would a small script or an AGENTS.md rule be the better artifact here?
Run the eval suite against both versions and give me a pass rate comparison before I decide which to keep.
What checks does this need to pass before I merge it into the shared repo and let other people install it?
Our runbook for the nightly reconciliation job is out of date since we moved to the new queue. Can you bring it back in line with what actually runs?
Write an ADR capturing why we moved off Celery and what we considered instead.
The API reference still documents the v1 auth header even though we shipped v2 months ago. Update it.
Rewrite the README intro so it's punchier and actually says what the project does in the first sentence.
Teach me how Kubernetes operators work — I want to work through it over several sessions.
Summarize where we got to on this refactor so a fresh session can pick it up tomorrow.
